subject.title: Question: supporting additional ChatGPT tools in browser mode

question: Should Oracle browser mode remain limited to Deep Research, or should it intentionally support a first additional ChatGPT composer tool or connected-app workflow?
rationale: The current implementation deliberately scopes support to Deep Research, and choosing a broader tool contract determines user expectations, permissions handling, and the maintenance burden of a rapidly changing external UI.

options.title: Keep the current boundary
options.body: Continue supporting Deep Research only and revisit broader tool selection when a concrete user workflow establishes a durable need.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow proof of concept
options.body: Select one named ChatGPT tool, define its expected availability and failure behavior, and validate it with a signed-in browser smoke before considering shared abstractions.

options.title: Adopt a general tool contract
options.body: Approve a maintained browser-mode capability layer for supported composer tools, including explicit compatibility and permission expectations.

recommendation.title: Keep the current boundary
recommendation.body: Continue supporting Deep Research only and revisit broader tool selection when a concrete user workflow establishes a durable need.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged Deep Research scope and browser-mode product direction most directly route to the person who merged that work.
